provenance: All content written for this project; not consulted against R-010 (מאל"ו) or R-013 (AnkiWeb).
source: data/amirnet-vocab.csv (Tier 1, A2) — K-005. Two groups: (a) 20 British/American spelling-variant headwords (behavior/behaviour, centimeter/centimetre, chili/chilli, colorful/colourful, criticize/criticise, gram/gramme, honor/honour, kilogram/kilogramme, kilometer/kilometre, labor/labour, license/licence, liter/litre, marvelous/marvellous, meter/metre, omelet/omelette, organize/organise, organized/organised, realize/realise, rumor/rumour, traveler/traveller), written under the American-spelling convention per lesson 38 in plan/80-content-lessons.md — these had been silently skipped by every prior tick's candidate-selection script because it filtered only on the space character and never handled the '/' in the CSV headword, leaving them sitting alphabetically BEFORE the recorded cursor ('impatient') without ever being picked up; found by re-deriving the missing-word list live against data/amirnet-vocab.csv and all batch-*.jsonl files rather than trusting the stored cursor (lesson 39). (b) 10 words continuing the alphabetical Tier 1 single-word sweep from the recorded cursor 'impatient' through 'invention'.
gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on the full draft via a scratch script (lesson 40), against allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt exactly as scripts/measure-gate.mjs and scripts/build-ingest-sql.mjs load it in production. Iterated to 0 gate failures and 0 background-word drift (a script-driven diff of every example/stem/distractor token against allowed-words, lessons 11/13/30/31/38). A 7-row negative control (one deliberately-broken row per failure class: level drift, Latin letters in translation, nikud in translation, fewer than 4 scorable distractors, stem with no blank, stem leaking the answer, headword missing from example) — 0/7 incorrectly passed. In addition: a mechanical a/an-agreement scan across every stem with a fixed article directly before the blank (lesson 44a) caught and fixed 3 leaks (omelet, instant, intelligent) where every distractor failed the article, making the correct answer guessable from the article alone; a full substitution printout (every distractor placed in every stem, lesson 44b) was read by hand and caught two idiomatic-collocation false positives not visible to any script — 'a quick bread' (omelet item 1, 'quick bread' is a real baking term) and 'acted impatient' (importantly item 2, 'acted' + bare adjective is itself grammatical) — both stems were rewritten rather than the distractors swapped, since the frame was the problem. Four Hebrew-translation collisions with already-shipped headwords were found by diffing this batch's translation_he values against every existing batch-*.jsonl (לבקר already used for 'visit', לארגן for 'arrange', להבין for 'understand'+'see', חרק for 'bug') and tagged with he_one_to_many_group on the new row (lesson pattern from 'hundred'/'century', C-0586); the older rows were left untouched rather than hand-edited, since retro-tagging a previously shipped batch file is a larger, separate edit this tick did not make unilaterally — flagged in the report for a future tick or PM decision on whether to backfill them.
batch_size_note: 30 rows. No per-batch ceiling since 09/09 (confirmed 12/09: spotCheckPlan() runs per-batch-file, not over the bank — the old 1,200-row/batch-of-12 caution was retired, per plan/80-content-lessons.md line 190: 'a batch of 12 rows when thousands of headwords are missing is not caution, it is the bottleneck'). 30 was chosen over a larger 40-style batch because roughly a third of this batch (the 20 spelling-variant words) required first re-deriving the true missing-word list from scratch against the live CSV and all 34 existing batch files rather than trusting the recorded cursor (lesson 39) — that investigation, plus the full real-gate + drift-diff + a/an scan + hand-read substitution printout + negative control on every one of 30 rows, was the size this session's window could verify end-to-end with the same rigor as the 40-row batches, without shortcutting the verification step itself.

A handful of hyphenated Tier 1 entries (good-looking, half-price, left-hand, make-up) were also left out of this batch pending confirmation that a hyphenated headword is schema-safe — untested, not confirmed broken.
